classification.difficultyReason: Reverse a target mean, then determine where an unknown sixth mark must lie in the ordered data before using the middle-pair median equation.

content.prompt: A student received the following marks for five tests: 75, 83, 74, 66 and 90.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Determine the minimum mark this student will need to receive on her sixth test in order to average at least 80.

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\text{Required total}&=6\times80\\\text{Required total}&=480\\\text{Minimum sixth mark}&=480-388\\\text{Minimum sixth mark}&=92\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: If the student’s median mark is 78 after six tests, determine the mark she received on her sixth test.

answer.short:
81 marks

Order the marks and use the average of the middle two values.
answer.worked:
The five known marks in order are $66,74,75,83,90$. A sixth mark at or below 75 would give a median at most 75; a mark at or above 83 would give a median of 79. Hence the sixth mark $x$ lies between 75 and 83, and the middle two marks are 75 and $x$.

$$\begin{align*}\frac{75+x}{2}&=78\\75+x&=156\\x&=81\end{align*}$$

Check: the ordered marks are $66,74,75,81,83,90$, so the median is $\frac{(75+81)}{2}=78$.
